name: REF01CSZ
title: Precision 10.0 V, 5.0 V and 2.5 V band-gap voltage references
summary: REF01 (10.0 V), REF02 (5.0 V) and REF03 (2.5 V) are series band-gap references that run from up to 36 V, draw at most 1.4 mA (1.6 mA for C grade) and source up to 10 mA (8 mA for C grade). A TRIM pin moves the output a few percent with an external potentiometer, and a TEMP pin gives an unbuffered voltage that tracks die temperature at about 1.96 mV/°C. Grades A, E, H and C differ in initial accuracy, drift and temperature range; REF01CSZ is the C-grade REF01 in 8-lead SOIC for −40°C to +85°C.
key_figures: 36.0 V absolute maximum; REF01 12 V to 36 V

notes: Models ending /883C are military-grade parts with their own data sheet.

Models with Z in the suffix (REF01CPZ, REF01HPZ, REF01CSZ, REF01CSZ-REEL, REF01CSZ-REEL7, REF02CPZ, REF02CSZ, REF02CSZ-REEL, REF02CSZ-REEL7, REF02HPZ, REF02HSZ, REF03GPZ, REF03GSZ, REF03GSZ-REEL7) are RoHS compliant.
REF02Z is the nongraded REF02 of the REF02 table.
The ADR01/ADR02/ADR03/ADR06 are pin-compatible successors with higher accuracy and stability over a wider temperature range.

circuits.title: Input and output capacitors
circuits.description: The reference with 0.1 µF ceramic capacitors from VIN to ground and from VOUT to ground. TEMP and TRIM are left open.

circuits.title: Optional output trim
circuits.description: A 10 kΩ potentiometer and a 1 kΩ resistor in series run from VOUT to ground; the wiper drives TRIM through 470 kΩ. Turning the potentiometer moves the output within the ranges of the trim-range table.

circuits.title: Temperature monitoring
circuits.description: An AD8641 wired as a unity-gain follower on 15 V buffers the TEMP pin, so the reference core sees almost no load; its output VTEMP moves about 1.9 mV/°C. TRIM is left open.

circuits.title: Burn-in circuit
circuits.description: The part runs between +18 V and −18 V for burn-in: VIN is fed from +18 V through 10 Ω, GND sits on −18 V, and each rail has a 10 µF capacitor to ground. A load resistor from VOUT to ground is optional; its current stays at or below 10 mA.

circuits.title: Basic reference application
circuits.description: The plain connection: supply on VIN with 0.1 µF to ground, output on VOUT with 0.1 µF to ground, TEMP and TRIM open. The capacitor values may be changed within the input and output capacitor guidance.

circuits.title: Simple current source
circuits.description: The reference floats on its load: RSET sits between VOUT and the reference's own GND pin, and that node, VL, feeds RL to ground. RL carries ISET = (VOUT − VL)/RSET plus the reference's quiescent current IQ of about 0.6 mA. Because IQ ranges from about 0.55 mA to 0.65 mA, the source suits low-precision use.

circuits.title: Programmable 0 mA to 5 mA current source
circuits.description: A REF02 on +12 V has its GND pin driven by an OP1177 on ±12 V. An AD5201 100 kΩ digital potentiometer sits across the reference (B at VOUT, A at the reference GND), and its wiper drives the op amp's inverting input; the non-inverting input sits on VL, the bottom of RSET (1 kΩ) and the top of the 1 kΩ load RL. The load current equals the voltage between the potentiometer's B and W terminals divided by RSET. The reference ground swings from −5 V to VL across the potentiometer's range, so the op amp needs both supplies.

parts.note: 100 kΩ digital potentiometer; ends A, B and wiper W; digital interface not drawn

notes: The output at VOUT spans 0 V to (5 V + VL); the reference ground spans −5 V to VL.

circuits.title: Precision boosted output regulator
circuits.description: An OP1177 on 15 V compares the reference output with VO and drives the gate of a 2N7002 through 100 Ω; the MOSFET passes current from VIN straight to the load. VO returns to the inverting input through 100 Ω, with 1000 pF from the op amp output to that input. The load shown is 200 Ω with 1 µF. With these parts it delivers up to 50 mA from a 15.0 V input; a larger MOSFET raises that.

circuits.title: Bipolar voltage reference
circuits.description: A REF03 gives +2.5 V; an OP97 inverting amplifier with two 100 kΩ resistors (gain −1) gives −2.5 V from it. The non-inverting input is grounded. A low-offset op amp keeps the negative output close to the positive one.
notes: OP97 pins: 2 inverting input, 3 non-inverting input, 4 negative supply, 6 output, 7 positive supply.

circuits.title: Negatively adjustable reference
circuits.description: A REF03 drives a 50 kΩ potentiometer to ground and, through 50 kΩ, the inverting input of an OP97 on ±15 V, which has 50 kΩ feedback. The potentiometer wiper sets the non-inverting input, so the output runs from −2.5 V with the wiper at ground to +2.5 V with the wiper at the reference output. The op amp supplies the load, so it needs low offset and enough output current.
notes: The op amp's positive supply pin is marked +15 V and is wired to the same V+ rail as the reference input.
OP97 pins: 2 inverting input, 3 non-inverting input, 4 negative supply, 6 output, 7 positive supply.

operation.text: A band-gap cell built from two NPN transistors whose emitter areas differ by two to one produces a PTAT current; added to one transistor's VBE it gives a nearly temperature-independent voltage VBG. An internal amplifier and resistor divider scale VBG to 10.0 V, 5.0 V or 2.5 V. Laser trimming sets the initial accuracy, curvature and drift.

No external capacitor is needed for stability, but 0.1 µF ceramic at the output is strongly advised for stability and low-level noise. Adding a 1 µF to 10 µF capacitor (ceramic, tantalum or electrolytic) at the output improves response to load steps at the cost of a longer turn-on. At the input, 1 µF to 10 µF helps where the supply moves, with 0.1 µF ceramic beside it against supply noise. Place all of them as close to the pins as possible.

TRIM moves the output either way from its factory value to cancel system errors such as line and load shifts, thermal hysteresis or reflow offset. With low-tempco trim resistors, trimming barely changes the reference's own temperature drift.

TEMP carries the PTAT voltage straight from the band-gap core, about 550 mV at 25°C and changing about 1.96 mV/°C. It is a convenience, not a precision sensor. Any current into or out of it disturbs VOUT: tens of microamps can pull the output out of regulation. A buffer amplifier with low input bias current, for example the AD8601 or AD8641, keeps the VOUT change below 100 µV.

Typical drift is about 50 ppm over 1000 hours of unloaded operation at +25°C, for every output voltage. It is not guaranteed and can exceed 50 ppm, mostly in the first 200 hours. Burning the part in, powered with or without a resistive load of at most 10 mA, reduces later drift.

The part sources up to 10 mA at room temperature over its whole input range. At high ambient temperature the input voltage and load current must be held so the dissipation stays within the package rating, which can mean less than the full load current.
Quiescent current stays constant as load current changes, which lets the part act as a current source with its ground pin floating on the load.

REF01 and REF02 come in A, E, H and C grades (and REF02Z, nongraded); A and E are the tightest in initial accuracy, C the loosest. A grade runs from −55°C to +125°C. C-grade drift and regulation are specified over 0°C to +70°C for the -J and -Z packages and over −40°C to +85°C for the -P and -S packages. REF03 has one grade, G. These figures cover commercial parts; 883 parts have their own data sheet.
After a temperature cycle the output at 25°C can differ from its value before; the shift comes mainly from package stress on the die and grows as the package shrinks.
